work.text: This format is called a pillar print, or hashira-e (literally, "pillar picture"). It is made by pasting two sheets together vertically to form a long, narrow picture, often hung as a decoration on the narrow support posts of the interior of Japanese houses.
Such tall narrow spaces are most difficult to handle. They stimulate what strength there is in a designer.

moment.text: They probably served as cheap alternatives to hanging scrolls (kakemono) which were typically made of silk.
Surviving examples are rare, and often faded, worn, or stained from exposure to soot and smoke.

matters.text: This print depicts a courtesan dreaming about the time she was taken from her family to become a courtesan. The man leading the girl by the hand is probably escorting her to the Yoshiwara, the entertainment district in Edo.
